headline_marked: Rod Johnson [[Brings AI Agents to Java]] with Embabel framework
headline: Rod Johnson Brings AI Agents to Java with Embabel framework
summary: The creator of Spring Framework returns with Embabel, a new AI agent framework for the JVM that focuses on goal-oriented agents and deterministic planning.
details: Rod Johnson, the influential creator of the Spring Framework, has returned to active development with Embabel, a new AI agent framework for the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). Unlike existing frameworks that center applications around the LLM, Embabel focuses on building goal-oriented AI agents that utilize deterministic planning.

Embabel is built on top of Spring AI, providing the low-level LLM plumbing, while Embabel itself offers the agent orchestration layer. This approach allows for more complex system behaviors beyond simple question-answering, such as agents that can perform multi-step tasks and adapt their plans based on outcomes.

The framework employs a Goal-Oriented Action Planning (GOAP) technique, similar to those found in video games. Each action has preconditions and effects, and a planner determines the sequence of actions to achieve a goal. This deterministic planning process provides an auditable trace, which is crucial for enterprise environments.

Developers can define actions with specific goals and let the planner figure out the optimal path. Actions can be annotated with `@AchievesGoal` to signify progress, and different LLM models can be assigned to different tasks using `withLlmByRole`, allowing for cost and capability optimization.

Embabel was first announced in June 2025 and publicly introduced in April 2026. It is currently in early access, requiring Spring Boot 3.5.x, Java 23, and an LLM provider API key. The framework is released as a SNAPSHOT, necessitating the addition of the Spring snapshot repository to project configurations.

The key advantage highlighted is Embabel's determinism. The GOAP planner provides an auditable trace of the agent's actions, offering a clear explanation for its behavior, a significant improvement over the often opaque decision-making of standard LLM chains. This auditability is a major draw for enterprise adoption.

topic: intel commits to 14a mass production in 2028 as its sales rise 25% year-over-year
headline_marked: Intel Commits to [[14A Mass Production]] in 2028 as Sales Rise 25%
headline: Intel Commits to 14A Mass Production in 2028 as Sales Rise 25%
summary: Intel plans to begin high-volume manufacturing using its 1.4nm-class process technology in 2028, aligning with TSMC's roadmap. The company reported a significant 25% year-over-year revenue increase.
details: Intel announced its commitment to mass production using its 14A (1.4nm-class) fabrication technology in 2028. This move aligns with TSMC's plans for its A14 process technology and follows a strong second quarter for Intel, with revenue reaching $16.1 billion, a 25% increase year-over-year.

The company aims for risk production of 14A for internal products in the second half of 2027, with high-volume ramp targeted for 2028. This typically means actual products manufactured with the technology would emerge in 2029, depending on the exact start date.

Intel's strong financial performance was driven by high demand for both client and data center products. The Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) saw revenue rise 13% year-over-year, primarily due to increased average selling prices (ASPs) rather than unit sales.

The Data Center and AI (DCAI) business showed the most significant growth, with sales climbing 59% year-over-year to $6.3 billion. This surge is attributed to strong demand for Xeon processors, expanding AI infrastructure, and growing sales of purpose-built silicon.

Despite a reported GAAP loss of $11 billion, largely due to mark-to-market losses on escrowed shares, Intel's non-GAAP net income was $2.2 billion, indicating profitable underlying operations. GAAP gross margin also improved to 40.1%.
